"We sold them a promise about consistency. I need to know by 15 November whether we keep it with people or with software, because Zoya will ask, and 'either' is not an answer that signs a ₹4.6 crore contract." — Gaurav Malhotra, email to Aparna Deshpande and Rukmini Nair, 6 October 2026
"If we put a curated tier on the price list, every customer in deciles two to ten asks why the standard tier is the uncurated one. We will have told 412 brands that what they have been buying is the version we do not stand behind." — Rukmini Nair, leadership meeting minutes, 12 October 2026
"Please don't quote the 18 per cent without the appendix. The arms are not comparable. I said this on the call." — Tanvi Krishnan, comment on the board deck draft, 21 October 2026
"Who signs off that this is good? That is my whole question. In my previous vendor it was a person with a name and a phone number." — Zoya Rahman, Al Qamra Retail Group, second diligence call, 8 October 2026

Section 7The options as Aparna currently frames them

Option one: Curate as a paid tier. Chhaap keeps Infinite Variants as the default and sells a curated seat — evaluator ranking plus human review by Lena's team — at ₹1.4 lakh per brand per quarter, launched with the top forty accounts and Al Qamra. Exhibit 5 says the blended revenue effect is minus 8 per cent, with the top decile falling 38 per cent, but Exhibit 5 assumes no churn change, which is the entire question. Rukmini's objection in the 12 October minutes is not commercial but semantic: naming one tier "curated" is a public statement about the other tier.

Option two: evaluator ranking on by default, for everyone, invisibly. The two hundred assets still exist; they are simply ordered, with the top ten surfaced first. No pricing change, no headcount, no positioning change, and Kabir can ship it in eleven days. It also means the standard embedded in the evaluator becomes, silently, the aesthetic of 412 brands, that "your brand, not ours" quietly stops being true, and that the region where the evaluator agrees with designers least is precisely the top of the distribution — the assets brands would actually publish.

Option three: refuse the automation and build a human editorial service. Twelve art directors, hired against the top forty accounts, with the evaluator used only as a first-pass filter. It answers Zoya's question with a name. It is slow to hire, it puts Chhaap in the agency business it defined itself against, and it is the option Aakriti has already proved can be sold — by Aakriti.

Aparna's discomfort, at eleven at night, is that all three options accept a framing she is no longer sure of: that the standard belongs to Chhaap. Nikhil's 0.22 correlation between designers and brand managers can be read as evidence that brand managers have poor taste, or as evidence that brand managers are optimising something Chhaap's designers do not see and have never asked about — reach on a Zepto thumbnail, say, or the fact that a Chandrika creative must sit beside a competitor's on a Nykaa results page. There is a fourth option in that reading — that Chhaap's product should help each brand write and apply its own standard, and sell that as the thing it does — but no one has costed it, no one has asked whether brand managers want that work, and it cannot be built by 15 November.

Section 8The deadline and the hard constraints

The board meets at 11 a.m. on Monday 26 October. A Series C term sheet is under discussion at a valuation anchored on the volume trajectory in Exhibit 2; the lead investor's diligence memo, which Aparna has read, uses assets generated as its primary growth measure. Al Qamra requires signature by 15 November for a January start, and Gaurav's consistency language is in the draft statement of work. Six of Chhaap's engineers remain committed to DPDP consent and provenance work until the end of December and cannot be moved. Contracts with 41 top-decile customers carry minimum generation commitments totalling 2.1 lakh assets a month, which any pricing change must either honour or buy out. Lena's team has nine people and no approved requisitions. And the festive quarter — Diwali on 8 November, followed by the wedding season — is Chhaap's highest-volume period of the year, which means whatever ships will ship into peak load.

Section 9Questions for discussion

1. What, precisely, is Chhaap selling today — generation, selection, or the appearance of both? Answer using Exhibits 2 and 5 rather than the positioning statement.

2. Exhibit 2 shows the published rate falling from 12 per cent to 3.2 per cent. List three distinct explanations consistent with the data as footnoted, and say what single piece of evidence would separate them.

3. Exhibit 3 and Exhibit 4 are both used inside the company to argue that the evaluator works. Take each in turn and state what it actually establishes, what it cannot establish, and what a hostile reader would say.

4. Nikhil's designer-to-designer agreement is 0.41 overall and 0.71 on the best work. What does that pattern imply about whether Chhaap has a standard at all — and does the same pattern strengthen or weaken Lena's position?

5. Rukmini argues that naming a curated tier tells 412 customers that the standard tier is not the one Chhaap stands behind. Is she right? What would you have to believe about customer perception, competitive positioning and the Series C narrative for her objection to be decisive rather than merely awkward?

6. It is Monday morning. What does Aparna recommend, what does she deliberately not decide yet, and what does she say to the board about the gap between the 18 per cent on the summary slide and the appendix beneath it?

Section 10Sunday, late

At around midnight Aparna put the forty-eight sheets back in order and found, without much effort, the four that Chandrika's brand manager had published. She had not chosen them herself beforehand, so it proved nothing; but three of the four would have been in her own set, and the fourth she would have rejected on sight. She sat with that for a while. She could not say, in a sentence she would be willing to put on a slide, why she would have rejected it, and she was aware that this was the entire problem she had been asked to solve and that she had fourteen hours left.

The evaluator, when she checked, had ranked that fourth asset eleventh out of two hundred and sixteen.
